title: Runtime Composer adapters: reference implementations for streaming tool pipelines with schema-enforced outputs
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Teams need concrete, idiomatic examples showing how to compose streaming model outputs, tool/function calls, and JSON-schema/typed outputs across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs while preserving backpressure, partial outputs, and compatibility with legacy sync clients.

Goal: Provide a small set of reference adapters ("Runtime Composer") and runnable examples that demonstrate: 1) streaming text + structured events that map to a JSON schema, 2) synchronous and async tool/function invocation patterns, 3) graceful fallback/shim behavior for older clients, and 4) recommended error-handling and backpressure strategies. These examples should be production-oriented (docs + tests + small e2e harness) and live in the SDK monorepo under examples/runtime-composer.

Success criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.
acceptance_criteria: TypeScript, Python, and Go examples compile/run with the current SDK release and include minimal README instructions.
Streaming example emits interleaved 'token' events and 'structured' events (schema-validated) and the consumer can reconstruct a typed object mid-stream.
Tool calling example shows both sync RPC-like calls (awaited) and background tool invocations that stream progress back to the client.
Compatibility layer: older sync-only clients can consume the final structured payload without breaking; documented shim included.
Bench test showing end-to-end latency with batching=auto and KV-cache enabled; numbers recorded in the PR description.
Automated tests for schema validation and backpressure behavior in CI (unit + small integration).
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SDK owners and runtime team. Scoped three canonical flows: (A) streaming text + schema events, (B) tool call + streamed progress, (C) sync shim for legacy clients.

2026-03-04: Prototype TS adapter (draft) that turns stream frames into typed events; initial approach uses an async generator + lightweight codec. Noted perf trade-off: per-frame JSON.parse cost impacts hot-path. Logged optimization follow-up to batch-parse frames (ENG-99910).

2026-03-06: Spike in Go to model backpressure behavior using channels. Found that the SDK's current streaming API drops messages if the consumer is slow; added buffering strategy doc and suggested changes to runtime backpressure flags.
2026-03-08: Review with PM and Design for API ergonomics. Design requested to expose 'eventType' discriminators on frames for easier UI wiring. PM asked for example mapping to Console timeline view.
2026-03-10: Opened PR #1213 with TypeScript and Python examples. PR shows an e2e harness against local runtime docker image. Requesting initial review from @morgan and @kai (runtime).

2026-03-12: Code review feedback: prefer schema validation at the SDK boundary (not only consumer). Implemented Ajv validation in TS example; Python example uses pydantic models. Added TODO to add Go schema validation with github.com/xeipuuv/gojsonschema.

2026-03-13: Discovered edge case where a tool call returns both streamed logs and a final JSON payload; added combinator that buffers final structured object while streaming logs to consumer. Documented in README and included test case.
2026-03-14: Security review triage: no secrets in examples, KMS/HSM flows out of scope. Marked security_review_required=false. Preparing release notes and coordination with docs for publication.
Next: finish Go validation, add CI integration tests, finalize PR and gather approvals for merge. Plan demo in SDK weekly on 2026-03-20.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: schema validation at SDK boundary increases CPU for high-throughput streams; compromise is opt-in validation with recommended presets.
Compatibility shim design: final structured payload includes metadata 'shim_compat_v1' that legacy clients ignore; new clients prefer event-stream consumption.
Performance note: when using per-token structured events, advise 'sampling' of tokens for validation to reduce overhead in high-volume production workloads.
Follow-ups: ENG-99910 (parse-batching optimization), ENG-99911 (runtime backpressure flags), PM-4482 (Console timeline mapping for structured events).
